extra.message: SQL injection in signup token validation — Attacker bypasses invite-code gating and can extract data from the registration_codes/other tables via injection in an unauthenticated endpoint. [verified: validate_token() f-string-interpolates code=form.registration_code.data into a raw text() query with no escaping; classic ' OR '1'='1 injection on the unauthenticated POST /signup endpoint bypasses invite-code gating and enables data extraction.]

Missing authorization on note deletion (IDOR) — Any authenticated user can delete arbitrary notes belonging to other users by POSTing to /notes/<id>/delete. [verified: Same delete_note() endpoint performs no authorization (CWE-862): the note is fetched by URL id and deleted unconditionally, allowing any authenticated user to delete other users' notes via POST /notes/<id>/delete.]

IDOR: delete any user's note — Any authenticated user can delete arbitrary notes belonging to other users (including admins) by iterating integer note ids, causing destruction of other tenants' data. [verified: delete_note() in routes/notes.py:44 does session.get(Note, note_id) then session.delete(note) with only @login_required and no note.user_id==current_user.id check; the ownership check exists only in home.html which merely hides the button, so any authenticated user can delete arbitrary notes by id.]

SSRF and local file read via profile image URL — Authenticated attacker can make the server fetch internal/cloud-metadata endpoints (SSRF) and read arbitrary local files via file:// (e.g. file:///etc/passwd), exfiltrating contents through their profile image. [verified: add_image (@login_required) passes form.url.data to get_base64_image_blob -> download -> urlopen with no scheme/host validation (ImageForm.url is a bare URLField+DataRequired), so file:// and internal http(s) URLs are fetched and base64-returned into profile_image, which templates render back.]

No rate limiting / brute-force protection on login — Attacker can brute-force passwords against the login endpoint without throttling or lockout. [verified: POST /login (do_login) accepts unlimited attempts with no throttling, lockout, or rate-limiting library configured in app.py or elsewhere, permitting credential brute-force.]

No rate limiting on login (brute force) — Attacker can brute-force user passwords without throttling or lockout. [verified: Same do_login handler has no rate limiting or lockout around the email/password bcrypt check; a search for any limiter/throttle/attempt control returns no matches, so brute-force is unthrottled.]

Missing CSRF protection on state-changing POST routes — An attacker who lures an authenticated user to a malicious page can perform state-changing actions as that user (delete notes, change account email/password/is_admin, alter preferences) without consent [verified: NoteForm uses plain wtforms.Form (not FlaskForm), no CSRFProtect is registered anywhere, and no SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE is configured, so state-changing POSTs like /notes/<id>/delete have no CSRF token validation and are exploitable via cross-site auto-submitted forms using the ambient session cookie.]

Broken access control: returns all users' non-private notes — Every authenticated user sees all other users' public notes on their home page; cross-user data exposure beyond intended scoping. [verified: get_notes_for_user(current_user.id) at utils/notes.py:9 filters or_(Note.user_id==user_id, Note.private==False), so every authenticated user's /home and /notes return all other users' non-private notes; with private defaulting to False (models/note.py), this leaks cross-user note content beyond the owner scope implied by the function name and per-user call sites.]

SQL statement logging via echo=True — Sensitive data (emails, query parameters, password hashes referenced in queries) is written to logs. [verified: models/__init__.py:15 sets echo=True on the app-wide engine, so all SQL—including the raw text() f-string queries in routes/signup.py and routes/account.py that embed user emails and search input—is written to stdout/logs. Hashes themselves aren't directly in queries but emails and query params are; this is a genuine but low-severity sensitive-data-logging misconfiguration.]

Account enumeration via signup response — Attacker can enumerate which email addresses have accounts, aiding targeted phishing/brute-force. [verified: do_signup flashes the distinct 'User already exists' message (line 62) when an email is registered, leaking account existence; this is reachable since the SQL injection in validate_token lets an attacker pass the code check to reach the enumeration branch.]
